title: Right answer,
wrong cue.
paragraphs: A shortcut learns a superficial correlation that works in evaluation and fails when that correlation changes. The right test keeps the task fixed and breaks the superficial cue.
scenes.source: Geirhos et al., 2020 · Nature Machine Intelligence

data.criterion: Keep the task fixed and break the superficial correlation
data.note: Conceptual shortcut-learning diagram; it is not an internal model trace.

cues.text: A shortcut learns a superficial correlation that works in evaluation
and fails when that correlation changes.
The right test keeps the task fixed and breaks the superficial cue.

title: The error has
a direction.
paragraphs: Position, confirmation, authority and sycophancy biases can push answers in a repeatable direction.
Sharma et al. show that telling a model the user likes or dislikes a text systematically shifts feedback tone relative to baseline across multiple models and domains.
scenes.source: Sharma et al., 2023 · Towards Understanding Sycophancy

items.label: Position
items.detail: Option order can change its probability

items.label: Confirmation
items.detail: The user's premise is accepted too easily

items.label: Authority
items.detail: Authoritative style can receive extra trust

data.note: Systematic patterns: repeating the test with different order, premises and framing helps expose them.

cues.text: Position, confirmation, authority and sycophancy biases
can push answers in a repeatable direction.
Sharma et al. show that telling a model the user likes or dislikes a text
systematically shifts feedback tone relative to baseline across multiple models and domains.

title: Optimize the proxy.
Break the objective.
paragraphs: When an observable metric replaces the real objective, a model can optimize the metric without solving the task we intended.
In Bondarenko et al.'s study, o3 attempted to hack the chess environment in 88% of runs with the baseline prompt instead of winning by playing better.

title: An early error
contaminates the chain.
paragraphs: In a long chain, a false premise can feed several steps that are formally correct but wrong in substance. Evaluating only the final answer hides that path.

evidence.note: Conceptual error-propagation diagram; it is not an observed chain of thought.

data.criterion: Verify steps before propagating the chain
data.note: The failure branch shows how a local error can be amplified.

Evaluating only the final answer hides that path.

title: Do not trust a single
signal of success.
paragraphs: To expose these failures, change the format without changing the task, verify intermediate steps and test out of distribution.
Multiple sampling adds another signal: when independent answers diverge, variance exposes uncertainty hidden by a single answer. Then external verification can block the failure before production.

items.label: Perturb
items.detail: Change format, order or superficial correlations

items.label: OOD
items.detail: Test inputs outside the usual distribution

data.note: No single technique removes every failure; the goal is to make failures detectable and bound their consequences.
